account:
Today I attended morning office business and the scheduled mill grain inspection, and I have now reached home ahead of noon lunch. The mill sales chest contained 82 hay bales and 92 emeralds. Nobody there supplied a direct explanation of the grain stores' condition, so my inspection establishes stock seen, not a fuller assessment.

The unusual feature is a persistent but vague report about a bridge or port change associated with the bakery. Several townsfolk repeat it; Townsfolk 11 mentioned that baker and freight were there. That is hearsay, not evidence that either proposed anything. I have heard no definite plan, purpose, or public announcement. Secretary has likewise found no firsthand proposal evidence from neighbour or freight, and no proposal in the office records checked. I cannot yet tell whether this concerns a real transport project or merely a circulating rumour.

Secretary is also trying to locate the town accounts ledger and the normal deposit place for council correspondence. Neither the appointment records nor treasury supplied those answers; the treasury held 128 emeralds. I authorized enquiries among town hall staff and expect a report at thirteen hundred.

A community gathering with innkeeper is confirmed for eighteen hundred in the great hall. Freight offered to escort me from the office, and I approved. I know of no confirmed connection between that gathering and the bakery report. My remaining scheduled business includes lunch, council letters at thirteen, tea with neighbour at fifteen, office at sixteen-thirty, the gathering, and home at nineteen.
